header: REGISTERED ONE-SHOT RUN - Track A, DynaSim exercise 1 (COLA -1pp, 2030 age profile). Python oracle benefits: not Axiom. Publishes regardless of outcome.

mortality_values.expected: A2 substitute, TR2008 intermediate, base year 2004, projection years 2009-2030

claiming_pmf.expected: the A3-pinned claim-age table (load_claiming_pmf), rows at or before 2008

realized_cola_history.expected: the committed realized COLA history for determination years 1979-2007 (before the first TR2008 rate year 2008; they enter levels only)

contribution_and_benefit_base_tr2008.expected: TR2008 V.C1 historical and actual rows (1975-2008)
contribution_and_benefit_base_tr2008.documented_differences_note: V.C1 prints projections from 2009; the oracle reads the realized bases for the observed careers (a named gap)

awi_before_1975.expected: the committed capture (the oracle's AWI before TR2008's 1975 start)

bend_points.expected: 42 USC 415(a)(1)(B) with the captured base amounts on the TR2008 intermediate AWI, eligibility years 1979-2030

delayed_retirement_credit.expected: the committed capture (42 USC 402(w) schedule and cap)

auxiliary_constants.expected: the committed capture (statute-cited spouse and survivor constants)

source_provenance.content_basis: sha256 over the persons and careers frames, each as its column names, dtypes and CSV text (pandas to_csv, no index, '\n' line ends)
sha256 over the persons and careers frames, each as its column names, dtypes and CSV text (pandas to_csv, no index, '\n' line ends)

provenance.basis: A2 proposed substitute (not adopted): SSA 2004 period life table x TR2008 V.A1 age-sex-adjusted death-rate ratio (projection year / base year) for the under-65 or 65-and-over group

R0.reduced_increases_definition: per member row (all draws pooled): the reduced increases in one PIA for the row's payment year.  An opening-stock person's count is on the opening record's clock.  A projected person's count is that of the own worker benefit when there is one, otherwise that of the deceased worker's PIA behind the widow(er)'s benefit.  A dually entitled person's spouse's or widow(er)'s amount rests on another PIA whose count can differ and is not shown here

component_shares_by_age_group.definition: per draw and age group: each selected component's share of the weighted baseline benefit total, sum_i w_i B_base[i, c] / sum_i w_i B_base[i], over the rows the tabulation receives; reported as the mean over draws in which the total is positive.  A1 section 16 asks for 'weighted component shares' without saying whether persons or amounts are weighted; this reports amounts, so a dually entitled person's components each count at their own amount

age.outside_groups: rows whose age falls in no group enter no cell and are counted in input_summary

benefit_period.label: calendar_year_payments
benefit_period.definition: benefit amounts are payments during the reference calendar year (annual model)

components.selected_benefit: B_s,i = sum of the scenario-s amounts of the selected components present in the row
components.sum_check: all components present must sum to benefit_base and benefit_reform (math.isclose)

membership.recipient_rule_definition: recipient in scenario s iff beneficiary_s is true and the selected-component benefit B_s is > 0
membership.identity_check_scope: every input row, including rows outside the age groups: recipient_base must equal recipient_reform
membership.membership_basis_definition: S_base = baseline recipients; S_reform = reform recipients; S_alt = recipients in both scenarios with B_base > 0
membership.flag_consistency: a row with beneficiary_s false and a positive benefit_s is refused
membership.decedents: not observable here: the supplied reference-period benefit decides membership

conventions.weights: the row weight, shared by both scenarios; finite, >= 0

statistics.ratio_of_scenario_means: 100 * (mu_reform / mu_base - 1), mu_s = sum_{i in S_s} w_i B_s,i / sum_{i in S_s} w_i (weighted ratio of scenario means)
statistics.mean_of_individual_ratios: 100 * (sum_{i in S_alt} w_i (B_reform,i / B_base,i) / sum_{i in S_alt} w_i - 1) (weighted mean of individual ratios)

conventions.unit: percent change of the reform relative to the baseline (negative = reduction); percent-of-scheduled = 100 + value

undefined_cells.full_sample: reported, never imputed (A1 section 7): a draw's cell with no members, zero total weight or a non-positive baseline mean has a null value and a reason; a group's draw summary for a statistic is defined only when every draw is, and otherwise has a null mean and SD with n_defined_draws and each undefined draw's reason; every other group and statistic is reported as usual

reasons.empty_baseline_membership: no baseline members, or zero total baseline weight
reasons.empty_reform_membership: no reform members, or zero total reform weight
reasons.empty_alternative_membership: no members in S_alt, or zero total S_alt weight

draws.reported_value: mean over draws of the per-draw statistic
draws.aggregation: mean = fsum(values) / K; sample_sd = sqrt(fsum((v - mean)^2) / (K - 1)) (ddof=1), the estimates.first_report._numeric_aggregate formula for K >= 2; sample_sd is null when K = 1
draws.scenario_pairing: each row carries both scenarios for one (draw, person); fixed paths and shared draws are upstream properties, checked here only through membership identity

floor.split_unit_definition: the opening-wave family unit (family_unit_id): every member of a family unit falls on one side (A1 section 16)
floor.splitter: populace_dynamics.harness.panel.split_panel_by_person(rows, 'family_unit_id', fraction=0.5, seed=seed) on the per-person-per-draw rows, so every draw of every person in a split unit falls on one side
floor.estimator_per_side: the reported value recomputed on the side: mean over all draws of the per-draw statistic; null if any draw's cell is undefined on that side
floor.floor: summary of |side_a - side_b| across the seeds where both sides are defined: mean, sd (numpy ddof=1), min, max, n_seeds, values; undefined seeds are listed in dropped_seeds; with fewer than 2 usable seeds the floor is undefined (null summary fields, defined false, undefined_reason), never zero
floor.source_convention: runs/replication_mermin_rows_v1.json conventions.floor, computed by scripts/replication_mermin_rows.py (seed_half_metrics, build_floors, reform_delta_diagnostic._summary)
floor.scale: half sample; not rescaled to the full sample
floor.deviation: A1 section 16: fewer than two usable seeds yield null summary fields, not the zero summary (no seed) or zero SD (one seed) of reform_delta_diagnostic._summary; and the split unit is the opening-wave family unit, not the Mermin-row person

conventions.acceptance_rule_note: none applied: the tabulation reports values only; Max ruled on 2026-09-23 that there is no numerical acceptance threshold (plan section 6 item 3)

components.sum_check: all components present must sum to benefit_base and benefit_reform (math.isclose)

membership.recipient_rule_definition: recipient in scenario s iff beneficiary_s is true and the selected-component benefit B_s is > 0
membership.identity_check_scope: every input row, including rows outside the age groups: recipient_base must equal recipient_reform
membership.membership_basis_definition: S_base = baseline recipients; S_reform = reform recipients; S_alt = recipients in both scenarios with B_base > 0
membership.flag_consistency: a row with beneficiary_s false and a positive benefit_s is refused
membership.decedents: not observable here: the supplied reference-period benefit decides membership

conventions.weights: the row weight, shared by both scenarios; finite, >= 0

statistics.ratio_of_scenario_means: 100 * (mu_reform / mu_base - 1), mu_s = sum_{i in S_s} w_i B_s,i / sum_{i in S_s} w_i (weighted ratio of scenario means)
statistics.mean_of_individual_ratios: 100 * (sum_{i in S_alt} w_i (B_reform,i / B_base,i) / sum_{i in S_alt} w_i - 1) (weighted mean of individual ratios)

conventions.unit: percent change of the reform relative to the baseline (negative = reduction); percent-of-scheduled = 100 + value

undefined_cells.full_sample: reported, never imputed (A1 section 7): a draw's cell with no members, zero total weight or a non-positive baseline mean has a null value and a reason; a group's draw summary for a statistic is defined only when every draw is, and otherwise has a null mean and SD with n_defined_draws and each undefined draw's reason; every other group and statistic is reported as usual

reasons.empty_baseline_membership: no baseline members, or zero total baseline weight
reasons.empty_reform_membership: no reform members, or zero total reform weight
reasons.empty_alternative_membership: no members in S_alt, or zero total S_alt weight

draws.reported_value: mean over draws of the per-draw statistic
draws.aggregation: mean = fsum(values) / K; sample_sd = sqrt(fsum((v - mean)^2) / (K - 1)) (ddof=1), the estimates.first_report._numeric_aggregate formula for K >= 2; sample_sd is null when K = 1
draws.scenario_pairing: each row carries both scenarios for one (draw, person); fixed paths and shared draws are upstream properties, checked here only through membership identity

floor.split_unit_definition: the opening-wave family unit (family_unit_id): every member of a family unit falls on one side (A1 section 16)
floor.splitter: populace_dynamics.harness.panel.split_panel_by_person(rows, 'family_unit_id', fraction=0.5, seed=seed) on the per-person-per-draw rows, so every draw of every person in a split unit falls on one side
floor.estimator_per_side: the reported value recomputed on the side: mean over all draws of the per-draw statistic; null if any draw's cell is undefined on that side
floor.floor: summary of |side_a - side_b| across the seeds where both sides are defined: mean, sd (numpy ddof=1), min, max, n_seeds, values; undefined seeds are listed in dropped_seeds; with fewer than 2 usable seeds the floor is undefined (null summary fields, defined false, undefined_reason), never zero

mortality.basis: A2 proposed substitute (not adopted): SSA 2004 period life table x TR2008 V.A1 age-sex-adjusted death-rate ratio (projection year / base year) for the under-65 or 65-and-over group

2011.psid_files_bundle_basis: sha256 of canonical JSON {path relative to the PSID data directory: raw sha256} (sorted keys, compact separators, trailing newline)

2009.psid_files_bundle_basis: sha256 of canonical JSON {path relative to the PSID data directory: raw sha256} (sorted keys, compact separators, trailing newline)

gaps.gap: TR2008 publishes no projected death probabilities by single age and sex; the A2 substitute (SSA 2004 period table x TR2008 V.A1 ASADR ratio, under-65 and 65+ groups, base year 2004) is used for 2011-2030 (2009-2030 for R6). It is proposed, not adopted; with base 2004 the 65+ ratio exceeds 1 in 2011-2012, and in 2009-2010, which only R6 projects

A4 nets non-DI mortality within the population model's cells; for the single-year A2 model these are single ages by sex, and a cell whose DI-origin expected deaths exceed the model's gives its other members probability zero. Infeasible cells are counted per draw (small invented cohort: many)

no earnings are drawn after the opening year, 2010 (2008 for R6; the certified forward law is fit for 2015-2022 from 2014); AIME uses the career from 1968 through the opening year with later years zero. Weights only
absent (zero in the AIME). Weights only

disclosed oracle approximation (the oracle's AIME over the career through the onset or death year, indexed to the second year before it, divided by 35 years with no elapsed or dropout years; PIA at that year's bend points); Max's ruling on decision 2(b) (2026-09-23, d074) for DI levels, and an A5 builder default for deaths before 62. Weights only

gaps.item: Disability clock for awards at 62 or later
gaps.gap: A4 exposes retirement claimants below FRA to DI awards; A5 keeps such a worker's eligibility clock at the year of attaining 62 (its reading of 415(a)(3)(B)(i) and 415(i)(2)(A)(iii)), not the award year the A1 section 6 table gives for a disabled worker; R2 keeps the award year. The DI benefit replaces the retirement benefit and carries no claim-age reduction. A1 does not address this case

not modeled for retirement or survivor benefits: a projected claimant whose career through the opening year gives a positive AIME has a positive oracle PIA and becomes a retired-worker beneficiary however few years it covers, and a widow(er)'s benefit does not check the deceased's insured status (A4 sets DI incidence per population, so DI awards never consult it). Membership and weights

gaps.item: Linked spouses outside the opening roster
gaps.gap: their deaths are not simulated, so their partners are never widowed in the projection, and with no career or simulated state in the cohort no spouse's benefit rests on their record (counted in the cohort diagnostics, and per row as spouse_outside_roster, or spouse_unlinked for a married claimant with no linked spouse)

a person whose opening-year Social Security (2010, or 2008 for R6) A3 could not observe (status unobserved) opens as a non-recipient, so any benefit is projected as a non-recipient's would be (a claim plan or an A4 award, on the career PIA) rather than carried from an observed amount (counted as ss_opening_year_unobserved in the cohort diagnostics and beneficiaries_ss_opening_year_unobserved per row)

gaps.item: Widow(er)s of workers who died before the opening wave
gaps.gap: the late spouse is outside the cohort and has no career, so a widow(er) not receiving in the opening year gets no aged-widow(er) benefit (counted as widow_deceased_outside_roster)
not projected (A4 models disabled workers only); only opening stock survivors still under 60 in 2030 carry the disabled_widow component
no marriage, divorce or remarriage is drawn after the opening year

A5 builder choices: aged widow(er)s entitled at the later of widowhood and 60; spouses at the later of their own claim and the worker's entitlement, at 62 or older. A disabled worker still entitled to DI draws no spouse's excess; one converted at FRA claims at the conversion

the oracle's realized series (policyengine-us, bound to the committed statutory capture), which equals TR2008 V.C1 for 1975-2008; for 2009 and 2010 the realized 106,800 differs from V.C1's projected 106,500 and 110,700 (recorded as documented differences). Only years through the opening year enter because no later earnings are drawn, so R6 reads none of the differing years

the Social Security reader resolves income years 2008, 2010 and 2012 only, so no 2009-wave recipient's first receipt can be bracketed: every 2008 recipient's receipt start is censored at 2008 (the R20 year-before-last item, about 2007, is not used). Retired workers' claim years are imputed at or before 2008, and the receipt-start clocks of disabled workers and of survivors and spouses under 62 are 2008 at the latest, before the first reduced increase (2009), so no reduced increase is lost (A1 section 6)
the M4 self-report comes from the 2009 wave only (the A3 default: the anchor wave, nearest the 2008 opening); later waves are not consulted
A1 rule 4 fixes the opening basis but does not mention recovery; A5 ends a disabled worker's opening basis at a simulated recovery
one plan per person drawn at 50+ from the 2008 table row (every projection year snaps to it); a plan age already passed claims in the next year. No claiming response to the reform
closed cohort: no entrants after the opening year
